I pulled frames 128, 130-138 and 140 at full resolution into /home/user/Youtube-videos/Future_Got_Weird/lightning-laser/source/out/qa_VA/ and built crop montages there: crops.png covers region (340,950)-(740,1350) and crops2.png is a closer zoom.

In f131 the tiny white fizz squiggles are starting at about (505,1200) but there is no disc. From f132 to f135 a flat, translucent lavender disc about 65-70 px across sits centred on the channel at about (505,1200). It has a uniform fill and a clearly hard circular rim, and the 4.36 fizz squiggles are drawn inside it (f133 and f135 at 2x zoom show this plainly). verdict.reading:
I pulled full-resolution frames 74, 76, 80, 84, 88, 92, 96, 100, 104 and 106, plus a crop of the branch region (x 460-720, y 590-920) for every frame from 70 to 108, and looked at them with Read.

**What the finding gets right.** From 75 to 105 the upper unguided branches keep exactly the same shape. Their brightness barely moves: pixels above 150 average 211.4-213.7, and the count of those pixels drifts slowly between about 4,075 and 4,627 (about ±6%) with no visible pulse. The lit cloud patch around the branch tops also looks the same in every top-half montage frame (76/84/92/100/104). Between consecutive frames the top half (y<900) changes by only about 0.9 mean absolute difference, and nearly all of that is rain streaks and the cyan packets. So the upper half is effectively held for about 1 s, as described.

**Why it hardly matters at normal speed.** The held area is never the only thing moving.
- Cyan packets travel up the laser line right through the branch area in every frame of the crop strip (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Youtube-videos/e9cf2999-ee74-59c9-a03c-f06d582b64e7/scratchpad/va/branches.png).
- Rain moves across the whole frame.
- The guided section below the branches is the brightest and largest part of the bolt, and its soft fronts climb continuously. That is where the eye sits.

A steady glow is also what continuing current physically looks like, and a short calm before the restrike at 106 makes that restrike hit harder. At frame 106 the branch region lights up hugely (about 74.6k pixels change by more than 15 in that crop).

**One detail is wrong.** In frame 88 (2.93 s), 'FOLLOWED' is already shown highlighted in yellow. So the hold falls during 'FOLLOWED', not just before it starts at 3.26.

**Verdict.** Real on a paused or measured basis, but a first-time phone viewer is unlikely to notice. No locked requirement is broken: the spec only asks for a slow flicker and soft fronts climbing the guided section, and those are present.

verdict.reading:
I could not refute this. I decoded frames 150-234 of the MP4 to grayscale at full resolution. I then measured frame-to-frame shift by phase correlation in five fixed patches: top (y40-300), bottom (y1400-1700), left edge, right edge, and a mid patch beside the leader tip (x400-650, y800-1050).

Between pops, the left, right and mid patches move a steady (-1,+2) px per frame, and the top patch moves (0..-1, +1..+2). At 175>176, 183>184, 190>191, 197>198, 205>206, 213>214 and 224>225 the motion breaks in a single frame: the top patch jumps (0,-8) to (+1,-9), the left patch (-2..-3, 0..+1) and the right patch (+3, -1..+1). At 190>191 the bottom patch jumps (0,+6). This is an outward radial jump of about 10 px relative to the drift, about 750 px from a centre near the tip, so roughly a 1-1.3% scale step. The mid patch by the tip keeps its normal (-1,+2) or (0,+1) through every pop. This matches the finding that the zoom is centred near the tip and the leader does not move.

My measurements do not show the cited pops at 179>180 and 209>210, but the other seven are clear. The settle after the dissolve is also uneven, as described. The top patch moves -20, -20, -10, 0, -10, 0, 0 px over 160>161 to 166>167, so it freezes at 163>164, jumps at 164>165 and freezes again.

In frame f197.png the sharp foreground N2/O2 molecules are spread over the whole frame, including the top and sides. The reviewer's anaglyph (qa_B/anaglyph_197_198.png) shows clear red/cyan fringing on the molecules at the pop that is absent in the reference pair.

The pops are not tied to the three scripted attempts (5.6, 6.35, 7.05 s). They come every 7-11 frames, about 3-4 times a second, which points to a stepped zoom rather than an intended punch-in.

I watched it muted from my own whole-film strip (film.png, every 12 frames), read every QA strip in film order, and checked full-res stills at frames 0, 54, 110, 233, 241, 588, 750, 1004 and half-res frames at 141, 147, 415, 429, 523, 547, 890 and 950. - **A (hook):** reads on a phone from frame 0. The cyan line runs through the rod tip (~465, 1420). The white-violet leader climbs it with a warm band ahead of it, connects at f54 with local cloud-base light and visible branching only past the guided section. - **C2 to C3:** packets run left to right through the optics and turn up the duct. The cut at f290|291 keeps the beam's angle and roughly its screen x. C3 is one continuous crane up the beam past the tower into one packet.

File check: ffprobe gives 1080x1920, 30/1, 1005 frames. qa/v3/audio_identity.json shows the REVIEW file's audio packets and PCM are identical to V2 (sha256 4c3f0b74... / 6a353e72..., lag 0), which matches V3_AUDIO_LOCK.md. I extracted f421, f429, f436, f445, f460 and f475 at full resolution, looked at f421, f429, f436 and f445, and measured the red-minus-blue warm profile across rows y=500 and y=960.

One part of the finding holds. At f429 (14.30 s, caption "and HEATING a narrow channel") the warm region is a broad, soft-edged diagonal swath. At y=960 its half-max extent runs from about x 293 to 963, so it fills about 62% of the frame width. At y=500 it runs off the right edge. With molecules this large on screen, it does not yet look like a thin channel. f421 is worse: the whole frame is a brownish haze with no clear band edges. So the brief's "readable as narrow by 'channel' (14.30)" is softly missed on that exact frame.

Two parts of the finding are wrong:
1. The cyan line is not in the left third of the band. At f429 it sits at x 586 on y=960, about 44% across the band. On y=500 it sits at x 708, about 52% across. That is close to the band's axis.
2. The band reads as narrow well before ~445. By f436 (14.53 s, the same caption still on screen) it is a clearly bounded diagonal strip, roughly x 450-960 at y=500. Its edges stand out against dark molecule-filled air, and the cyan line runs inside it. It keeps tightening through f445 (about x 380-870), f460 (about 410-736) and f475 (about 430-716).

The narrowing is one continuous pull-back that resolves within about 0.2 s of the word "channel", while the caption is still up. At normal speed on a phone, a first-time viewer sees a warm band tighten around the cyan line as they hear "narrow channel". They would not notice a contradiction. This is a nit against the shot brief, not something a viewer would flag.

The file checks out with ffprobe: 1080x1920, 30/1, 1005 frames. qa/v3/audio_identity.json is present and lists the same video stats.

I extracted full-resolution frames 878, 881, 884, 887, 890, 893, 896, 899, 902 and 910 to /home/user/Youtube-videos/Future_Got_Weird/lightning-laser/source/out/qa_VALL/ and viewed f878, f884, f890 and f910.

Part of the finding holds up. In f878 the warm element is only a faint smudge just above the rod tip. In f884 and f890 it is clearly a soft, feathered oval glow hugging the cyan line above the tip. It is visibly fuzzier and wider than the thin, defined band with cyan packets inside it in f910.

I measured the warm extent (R minus B above 15) along rows y = 600 to 900:
- f881 to f890: about 100 to 125 px wide at full resolution.
- f893 to f899: about 80 to 90 px.
- f902: about 70 px.
- f910: about 57 to 60 px.

So the band does start wider and softer and narrows steadily over about 0.6 s, which supports the "wider and fuzzier" part.

The "sits left of the cyan line" part does not hold. At every measured row from f884 to f910, the warm-weighted centroid lies within 0 to 2 px of the cyan line. Examples:
- f890: centroid 607 vs cyan 606 at y = 700, and 578 vs 576 at y = 800.
- f887: centroid 599 vs 596 at y = 700.

The only offsets are at the extreme lower end of the shape. In f881 at y = 800 the centroid is 12 px right of the line, not left. In f887 at y = 900 it is 14 px right, also not left. No frame shows the shape displaced left of the beam.

At normal speed, during the tilt-up on "EXTENDED one", the shape reads as warm light growing along and centred on the beam and tightening into the familiar band within about half a second. That fits a channel forming and extending. A first-time phone viewer is unlikely to read it as unrelated haze or notice that the band style differs briefly.

Overall this is a real but cosmetic softness and width difference for about 0.4 to 0.6 s, the claimed off-axis placement is refuted, and no locked requirement is broken. Severity: nit.
